title: Canonical NDC v2 Profile 1 record envelope — version 1
description: One canonical JSON object per LF-terminated record line. The ordering member is a tagged union: exactly one of sequenced or reference, never both. The ordering key is NOT trusted from a caller field; it must be recomputed from the canonical record bytes. See ordering-profiles.schema.json and semantic-constraints.md.

SequencedOrdering.description: Sequenced mode. Domain and epoch must match the containing artifact's sequenced record_order_profile.

ReferenceOrdering.description: Reference mode. The containing artifact's record_order_profile must be the reference profile.

value.description: Scalar text interpreted by kind; boolean is the literal true or false, bytes_hex is lowercase hexadecimal. No binary floating point is admitted.

Payload.description: Strict abstract payload container. Authoritative member names and types for each event type come from the versioned per-event-type payload schema registry; an unregistered event type fails closed.

ordering.description: Tagged union; exactly one kind. Both key sets on one record are rejected because neither tagged branch permits the other branch's members. SEMANTIC CONSTRAINT (not expressible in JSON Schema): the producer must parse the canonical record bytes, extract the ordering fields from those parsed bytes, validate the mode and domain/epoch against the containing artifact profile, derive the ordering key from the validated parsed values, sort by that derived key, then serialize and emit the same validated canonical bytes. The verifier independently repeats parse/extract/validate/derive/check on the received bytes. No caller-supplied order key, position, index or pre-sorted hint is trusted. A key that does not recompute from the record bytes is rejected on both sides. Event time is never a sort key and there is no fallback to event time.

RecordEnvelope.description: Canonical record envelope. One RFC 8785 JCS object per LF-terminated line; no BOM, CR, blank line or incomplete trailing record.
